name: Lisa Escárcega

summary.text: Lisa Escárcega is the incumbent State Board of Education member for District 1. She is a retired educator and former executive director of the Colorado Association of School Executives.

experience.text: Colorado State Board of Education, District 1 (incumbent).
Executive director, Colorado Association of School Executives.
Ph.D. in quantitative research methods, University of Denver; master's and education specialist degrees from Ball State University; bachelor's degree in psychology from Northern Michigan University.

education_focus.text: Escárcega says she would keep pushing the state's early-literacy gains into middle school and use school accountability 'to help schools, not just label them.'
On funding, she says Colorado's school finance formula 'is not enough to provide adequate funding' and supports changing state tax rules through Proposition NN and Amendment 87.
On homeschool enrichment funding, she says 'public dollars should stay within the system' and should not be 'siphoned off' by privately run enrichment programs.

record.title: Social studies and math academic standards revisions
record.detail: Escárcega says she 'already helped make significant changes to the social studies and math standards' as a board member and would continue updating math standards to add alternative pathways.

positions.source_title: 9 questions for Colorado's State Board of Education candidates this year
positions.quote: Yes. Our school funding formula, even the new one being implemented, is not enough to provide adequate funding for a strong Colorado education system.
positions.note: Answering Chalkbeat's combined question on whether she supports 'changing state tax rules to raise more money for education, as proposed in Proposition NN and Amendment 87'; her 'yes' covers both measures.
